reason: E1 directly supports a layered oxide sequence (Ni-rich, Cr-rich, Fe/Mn/Co-rich) in an equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn alloy at 400°C/10 mbar O2, but it does not address the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 composition, the role of Ti, or behaviour under reducing atmospheres. E2 discusses general corrosion resistance and Al effects on phase stability but provides no specific evidence on oxidation layering, diffusivities, or reducing-gas behaviour. Thus, only the general concept of a layered oxide is supported, while the other premises lack direct evidence.
premises: Sequential, element-specific oxidation produces a layered oxide scale in fcc CCAs at ~400°C
Ni diffuses fastest and forms an initial Ni-rich pre-oxide layer
The Ni-rich layer promotes nucleation of a protective Cr2O3 mid-layer
Slower-diffusing Fe, Co, Ti form an outer, less protective oxide that causes spallation
Reducing atmospheres suppress oxide formation and preserve the layered structure
